normalized.description: The Advanced Power Architecture (APA) is a standard concept for the Power Conditioning and Distribution Unit (PCDU). APA follows the interoperable and interchangeable modularity approach applied for the project ADHA (Advanced Data Handling Architecture) that started in 2020. APA is aimed to be fully compatible with ADHA so that together they will form the kern of a satellite platform.As ADHA, APA is composed of two elements: a standardized Unit rack (element 1) that providesstandard services to a set of Power Modules (element 2) that populates the rack to make an APA PCDU. The power unit can be built upon modules from different manufacturers, based on performances, cost, programmatic constraints. This approach allows strong reduction of development time and recurrent costs, faster development and adoption of more performing technologies in great part enabled by the envisaged interoperable and interchangeable modules that compose the system.The definition the Advanced Power Architecture and related Standardization of the development ofthe APA element 1 (rack product) is being addressed in a dedicated activity funded by the Preparation Element of the DPTD and by the Future EO Program (ESA/IPC(2022)1,add.42). The modules that compose the element 2 of the APA are subject to several TDE activities. Element 1 outputs (APA Unit requirements and standard requirements for APA Modules) will be used as inputs to Element 2 activities. Element 2 outputs (APA Modules) will then be used as input to Element 1 (for the validation of standard power modules requirements and overall APA architecture).GaN advantages (e.g. high switching frequency, thermal performance, inherently radiation tolerant),allowing a more compact power cell, will be fully exploited in combination with resonant power conversion techniques. Digital control techniques provides flexible and reliable control of the power cell and a first level failure detection isolation and recovery (FDIR)in the module.This activity aims to develop the Solar Regulator module (SAR) for battery buses with Maximum Power Point Tracking capabilities.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Consolidation of APA Requirements (generic and specific modules)- Trade off and evaluation of the most promising Conversion Power Cell topologies- Preliminary and detailed design definition- Manufacturing and testing the module- Contribution to the APA Unit integration and test, including APA standardised documentationand interoperability/interchangeability test.
